newsitem.title: UK: Gulf Canada says Clyde bid 30p overvalued.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada says Clyde bid 30p overvalued.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources said on Tuesday that its raised offer for Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc of 120p per share was 30p overvalued.
Speaking to reporters after it raised its offer from 105 pence per share, president and chief executive officer J.P. Bryan said the new offer was "very attractive and aggressive."

He said Gulf Canada had accepted the asset valuation of 120 to 140 pence for Clyde put forward by Clyde's consultants "despite the fact that it is 50 percent above the net asset valuations by independent analysts."
He said these put Clyde's net asset value at around 90 pence per share, but addded "we are willing to pay a stretegic premium to be successful in this offer."
Bryan said there was a danger that Gulf Canada could pay too high a price for the British company.
"Gulf could be paying too much if commodity prices go into a downdraft. That is a risk we are prepared to take," he said.
He said Clyde's own strategy for growth was a "difficult one," which relied too heavily on the exploitation of the 9/14b block in the North Sea.
"Clyde has no experience as an operator and limited experience at drilling horizontal wells. This is a very thin reed on which to build future value and this is highly speculative," Bryan said.

Gulf Canada said "there wasn't a sniff or a rumour" of a rival bid emerging. "I can't see that anyone could possibly find justification for making a higher bid unless it is based on synergy or insanity," Bryan said.
Bryan said there would be no job losses at Clyde as a result of its acquisition. "Our plan is to grow this in a very aggressive fashion. We hope to employ more people."

Dick Auchinleck, a senior vice president of the company, added that Gulf Canada's record in Indonesia, where it achieved "significant growth " from assets similar to Clyde's, would serve as a model for the British aquisition. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
